hero.headline: Juno Beach debates reinstalling fence at JB-7 beach access after resident complaints
hero.teaser: Residents at the Colony Condos say beachgoers are cutting through their private property since Juno Beach removed a fence at the JB-7 public walkway in 2023. The town council will take up the fence question during budget discussions on July 15.
hero.body:
A dispute over a missing fence at a public beach access point in Juno Beach is creating friction between condo residents and summer visitors. The town removed the fence at the JB-7 walkway in 2023 for safety reasons, but residents at the Colony Condos now say the removal has created problems. With only bushes marking the boundary between public access and private property, residents report that beachgoers are regularly cutting through their land.

Lori Hill, a Colony resident, described the impact during peak summer months. "Lots of cars that just come at random, and then they just park on the spots there," Hill said. "Bushes are pushed back that they cut through those with their coolers and their fishing rods and lawn chairs and everything, and then they just park there all day." Hill said residents used to directly confront trespassers about being on private property, but those interactions often turned confrontational. Now, residents call police to handle the situation instead. The repeated trespassing has made the boundary between public and private land unclear to beachgoers.

Not all beach users agree there is a serious problem. Michael House, a beachgoer who walks to JB-7 from a public parking lot blocks away, said he has not witnessed the problems residents describe. "There's plenty of free parking. If they're damaging property and you know littering and stuff like that might be a different issue," House said. "I have never noticed anyone hopping the fence or the shrubs or anything like that."

The issue was brought before the Juno Beach Town Council, where a town official noted that the town is not legally required to install a fence. Vice Mayor Pro Tem DD Halpern suggested exploring lower-cost alternatives. "I understand fencing is expensive, but I'd like to see maybe we can help them with a lower-cost fence or some combination of split rail and shrubs," Halpern said. Residents hope the town will reinstall the fence to restore clear property lines and protect their landscaping and parking areas. The town council agreed to address the question during its budget discussions scheduled for July 15. A full replacement fence could cost the town six figures, making the decision a significant budget consideration.

cards.headline: DeSantis allies accuse Lieutenant Governor Jay Collins' wife of running anonymous accounts attacking Governor
cards.teaser: Multiple X accounts were suddenly deactivated Friday after allegations surfaced that they were tied to Layla Collins, wife of Lieutenant Governor Jay Collins, a.
cards.body:
Multiple X accounts were suddenly deactivated after allegations surfaced that they were tied to Layla Collins, wife of Lieutenant Governor Jay Collins. The accusations came from prominent veterans of Governor Ron DeSantis' communications team, including Christina Pushaw, a communications specialist in the Governor's Office, and Jeremy Redfern, Deputy Chief of Staff to Attorney General James Uthmeier. Pushaw shared information posted by Promota CEO Robert Salvador showing the account @FSUdude01670 appeared connected to a phone number similar to a known number and email used by Layla Collins. Florida Politics obtained screenshots verifying this through two-factor authentication, which can be triggered when an individual attempts to access an account without the preset password or if the social platform deems the password compromised. Screenshots showed an access attempt triggered a message to an email address with letters starred out and to a phone number with only the last digits visible.

Pushaw identified a second account, @bobnamy1, that she said also appeared tied to Layla Collins. She noted the account's content consisted entirely of promoting Jay Collins and attacking people who did not endorse him, including the governor. Redfern corroborated the claims, posting that "The FSUDude account was tied directly to her personal cell phone number." Both accounts were deactivated after Pushaw and Redfern publicly leveled their criticisms. Florida Politics has requested comments from Jay and Layla Collins.

cards.headline: Martin County School Board fights judge's order to reinstate teacher suspended over Charlie Kirk Facebook comments
cards.teaser: The Martin County School Board filed a court challenge Thursday against an administrative law judge's recommendation to reinstate a teacher who was suspended la.
cards.body:
The Martin County School Board filed a court challenge Thursday against an administrative law judge's recommendation to reinstate Matt Theobald, a social studies teacher at Spectrum Academy since 2009 who was suspended following Facebook comments about conservative activist Charlie Kirk. In the filing, the school board argued that Administrative Law Judge Jodi-Ann Vanessa Livingstone made "numerous findings" that "are not based upon competent substantial evidence." The board's attorney contended that Theobald's Facebook post labeling Kirk as racist, misogynistic and a neo-Nazi was a "serious offense" and that removing him was appropriate.

According to an investigation report, Theobald admitted writing the comments but said they were posted on his mother's private Facebook page "within a discussion among personal acquaintances" and were not intended for public view. In an order issued last month, Livingstone cited a recent Florida Fifth District Court of Appeal ruling stating that disciplining a teacher for personal Facebook posts made off school grounds, on personal equipment, with no student involvement, violated the teacher's First Amendment rights. Livingstone also recommended Theobald be awarded back pay and benefits. The school board retains final authority on whether Theobald returns to his position, though the timeline for a decision remains unclear.

Lt. Brett Harry said the teams will respond to emergencies ranging from stubbed toes to cardiac events and potential spinal injuries. cards.headline: St. Petersburg selects $8.1 billion plan to redevelop Tropicana Field site around civic park and museum
cards.teaser: St. Petersburg Mayor Ken Welch selected The Burg Bid as the preferred plan to transform Tropicana Field and the Historic Gas Plant District into a mixed-use district centered on a 13-acre civic park.
cards.body:
St. Petersburg has chosen The Burg Bid, a proposal led by Blake Investment Partners and Related Group, as its preferred path forward for transforming Tropicana Field and the surrounding Historic Gas Plant District. The $8.1 billion plan would convert stadium parking and public land into a mixed-use neighborhood featuring housing, hotels, offices, retail, cultural institutions, workforce training, public art and entertainment venues. The development team proposes purchasing 58 acres of city-owned land for $275 million, valuing the full land package at $405 million when including $130 million in land the city would retain. They plan to deposit $20 million when a purchase and sale agreement is finalized.

The proposal centers on Samuel Davis Park, a 13-acre central green space designed to serve as a civic and cultural hub rather than organizing around a new stadium as previous plans had done. The park would anchor 18.5 acres of total public park space and house The Woodson African American Museum of Florida, a planned Museum of Public Art, a Discovery Center, event lawns, a playground, a splash pad, cafe areas, public art and a concert lawn. The Woodson would serve as "an anchor and a civic landmark for the Gas Plant District," positioned within Samuel Davis Park along a diagonal pedestrian corridor called the Legacy Link. The proposal heavily emphasizes the history of the former Gas Plant neighborhood, a predominantly Black community demolished decades ago to build the stadium. Plans include preserving the original gas tank footprint, restoring Booker Creek from its current state as a drainage ditch, and constructing nine bridges as a reference to the nine bridges that once connected the historic area. A reimagined Pinellas Trail would integrate with wide pedestrian paths and a community park along the creek.

The development calls for 3,600 income-restricted housing units built over 15 years, with 1,800 units in the Historic Gas Plant District and another 1,800 on complementary sites elsewhere in St. Petersburg. The plan also includes homeownership opportunities at discounts to market value through partner Blue Sky Communities, a Florida-based affordable housing developer. The district would be constructed in three phases lasting approximately five years each, with early development potentially beginning outside the Tropicana Field footprint before stadium demolition. The Rays' lease ends after the 2028 season.

Phase 1 would establish cultural and workforce anchors including the Woodson and the Collaboratorium, a workforce training and small-business development center operating as "St. Petersburg's Capital Factory." Phase 2 would develop new mixed-income neighborhoods and strengthen connections with adjacent districts. Phase 3 would complete the neighborhood with a 4,000 to 5,000-seat Resilience Event Center featuring 100,000 square feet of flexible space for concerts, performances and events, plus a Discovery Center and St. Pete Surf Wave attraction.

cards.headline: Riviera Beach named only Florida city to receive 2026 All-America City Award
cards.teaser: Riviera Beach was selected as one of just 10 communities nationwide to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League. The award recognizes communities that bring residents, local government, businesses and organizations together to solve local challenges.
cards.body:
The City of Riviera Beach was named one of just 10 communities in the U.S. to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League, and was the only Florida city selected for the honor this year. The award was announced during the National Civic League conference in Denver, where Riviera Beach leaders presented the city's efforts to strengthen community engagement. Mayor Douglas Lawson said "Little old Riviera Beach is one of the biggest, brightest, shining stars." Lawson said the city earned the award through a long-term effort to revitalize Riviera Beach and improve quality of life for residents, noting that residents are "seeing the changes; they're seeing the revitalization and the reimagining of Riviera Beach."

The award recognizes communities that bring residents, local government, businesses and organizations together to solve local challenges and create lasting change. Riviera Beach's application highlighted several programs including the Riviera Beach Youth Council, the Citizens Leadership Academy with a 98 percent completion rate, and the Neighborhood Reclaim Home Rehabilitation Program. Councilwoman KaShamba Miller-Anderson said the award is "a tribute to the heart and determination of our residents" and that winning reinforces community pride. The All-America City Award has been presented annually since 1949 and is considered one of the nation's most respected civic honors.

cards.headline: Boca Raton High School band to represent Florida in National Independence Day Parade
cards.teaser: The Boca Raton Community High School band will march in Washington D.C.'s National Independence Day Parade on July 4. The students will march a full mile along the National Mall, representing the entire state of Florida.
cards.body:
The Boca Raton Community High School band has earned a coveted spot in Washington, D.C.'s National Independence Day Parade, representing the entire state of Florida. On July 4 at 10:30 a.m., the students will march a full mile along the National Mall, from Constitution Avenue to Independence Avenue. Only bands nominated by state officials receive invitations to this prestigious event.

Junior Lola Cabezas acknowledged the scale of the event, noting there are millions, if not billions, of people watching. She explained that most people don't realize how physically demanding marching band is, as performers must play, breathe, and walk while maintaining a consistent sound. Senior Stephin Restivo said the team is focused on the marching and timing of everything, adding that everyone will be able to see what the Boca High band is capable of. Band Director Jenn Girdlestone expressed full confidence that her students will put their best foot forward and represent the country well. Senior Lily Schaffer called the opportunity amazing, saying it shows how much the program has grown. The parade will be streamed live on YouTube for those who want to cheer on the band from home.

cards.headline: S.D. Spady Elementary in Delray Beach jumps from C to A rating
cards.teaser: S.D. Spady Elementary School in Delray Beach made a dramatic leap from a C rating last year to an A this year, part of Palm Beach County schools earning a third consecutive A rating from the state. The district saw 143 schools rated A or B, up from 120 the previous year.
cards.body:
The School District of Palm Beach County earned an "A" rating from the state for the third year in a row, with 143 district-operated schools receiving "A" or "B" ratings, up from 120 schools the previous year. One of the biggest success stories came from Delray Beach, where S.D. Spady Elementary School made a dramatic leap from a "C" rating last year to an "A" this year. Community member Chris Ceasar, who attended Spady as a child and now has family members enrolled there, said the jump from a C to an A school is huge and important for the community.

Principal Rona Tata, who has spent 15 years as principal after serving five years as assistant principal, said lots of work went on behind the scenes. The school had an A rating two years ago and narrowly missed a B rating last year by just a few points. Three years ago, staff began modifying the school's early childhood curriculum program, which starts at age 3 and combines with kindergarten. Many of those students are now in third grade and performing at higher levels. S.D. Spady Elementary was one of four district schools to improve from a C rating to an A this year. The others include Dwight D. Eisenhower K-8, Glade View Elementary and West Gate Elementary.

cards.headline: Hobe Sound community raises funds for man who lost fiance in deadly home fire
cards.teaser: Friends in Hobe Sound have launched a fundraiser to help Mark rebuild after a fire Monday killed his fiance, Misty Dawn White, 46. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office point to an electrical issue as a possible cause.
cards.body:
A Hobe Sound man is leaning on his community after losing his fiancée in a deadly home fire earlier this week. Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside the couple's home. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office point to an electrical issue as a possible cause. The fire remains under investigation.

Nina Fenn, a friend of White's for eight years, learned of the death through a phone call from White's fiancé, Mark. Friends have since launched a fundraiser to help Mark rebuild after the flames destroyed many of his and White's belongings. Fenn described the situation as "completely a state of devastation." She reflected on White's character, noting that "Misty was a Christian woman. She loved gardening and plants. She plays the piano" and "was always the first to lend a hand." Fenn said the loss is compounded by grief Mark has already endured, as he lost his only child, Jacob, tragically. White's death adds another layer of heartbreak, as her birthday is the Fourth of July and she passed just days before turning another year older. "She's always been a good soul to me. She'll always be in our hearts," Fenn said.

cards.headline: Breast cancer patient speaks out after insurance denies reconstruction surgery hours before procedure
cards.teaser: Beth Clark, 48, and her surgeon are speaking out after Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield denied coverage for a breast reconstruction procedure less than 24 hours before it was scheduled. The denial involved a surgical mesh called GalaFlex that insurers say is still investigational.
cards.body:
Beth Clark, 48, was diagnosed three months ago with invasive ductal carcinoma, the most common type of breast cancer. She chose to undergo a full double bilateral mastectomy with reconstruction. Clark completed the mastectomy, but less than 24 hours before her reconstruction surgery, her insurance company, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield, denied coverage for the procedure. According to her denial letter, the surgery, which involved a surgical mesh called GalaFlex, is still considered "investigational" and "there is no or not enough proof it improves health." GalaFlex is a synthetic surgical mesh approved by the FDA for some uses in the body but not for breast reconstruction. In a 2023 letter to health care providers, the FDA stated that the product's "efficacy and safety for breast cancer patients have not been determined."

Dr. Alicia Billington, Clark's plastic surgeon, uses GalaFlex mesh on most of her breast reconstruction patients and says it produces the least amount of complications compared to other options. Billington has publicly criticized insurance denials and recently shared Clark's case on social media. Last year, after investigative reporting, Cigna became the first and only major insurer to approve GalaFlex for breast reconstruction. Despite Anthem's denial, Clark received her reconstruction surgery with the GalaFlex mesh a little more than a week ago through a mechanism Billington arranged. An Anthem spokesperson said the company regularly reviews coverage policies to ensure they align with medical evidence and treatment standards, but the mesh does not currently meet their medical policy requirements without FDA approval. Clark and Billington are continuing to fight the denial.

hero.headline: Hobe Sound woman dies in house fire days before birthday, community rallies around fiance
hero.teaser: Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside the Hobe Sound home she shared with her fiance. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office point to an electrical issue as a possible cause.
hero.body:
Misty Dawn White, 46, died in a house fire at her Hobe Sound home on Monday. Investigators from the sheriff's office have preliminarily identified an electrical issue as a possible cause, though the investigation remains ongoing. White's fiancé Mark learned of her death and has since received support from their community as he faces the aftermath of losing both his home and his future wife.

Nina Fenn, who had been close friends with White for eight years, learned about the tragedy through a phone call from Mark. Fenn later returned to the scene to process her grief and has been vocal about supporting Mark during this difficult time. "It's just a terrible shame and awful loss of life," Fenn said. Friends have organized a fundraiser to help Mark rebuild his life after the fire destroyed many of his and White's belongings. According to Fenn, "It's completely a state of devastation."

Fenn shared memories of White that paint a picture of a generous and caring person. White was a Christian woman who had many passions, including gardening, plants, and playing the piano. Fenn recalled that White was always willing to help others. "She was always the first to lend a hand. She loves kids; she loves her kids. She loves people," Fenn said. Those who knew White hope to keep her memory alive through the impact she made on their lives. "She's always been a good soul to me. She'll always be in our hearts," Fenn said.

The timing of White's death has compounded the tragedy. Her birthday fell on the Fourth of July, meaning she passed away just days before celebrating another year. The loss is made more difficult by Mark's previous hardship. Fenn explained that Mark had already endured significant grief when he lost his only child, Jacob, in a previous tragedy. "Mark lost his one and only child, Jacob, and lost him tragically. So, I just am trying whatever I can to support him," Fenn said. As the community continues to rally around Mark, those who knew and loved White are finding solace in remembering her spirit and generosity.

cards.headline: Stuart downtown dock closes Sunday for $3 million renovation to nearly double boat slips
cards.teaser: Stuart's downtown public dock will close July 6 for renovations projected to be complete by next Fourth of July. When finished, the project will expand from 18 to 44 slips for both motorized and non-motorized vessels.
cards.body:
Stuart's downtown public dock will close July 6 for a $3 million renovation projected to be complete by next Fourth of July. The project will nearly double the dock's capacity, expanding from 18 to 44 slips for both motorized and non-motorized vessels. The renovation will include a 7,500 square foot fixed dock, a 1,400 square foot floating dock and a smaller floating platform. The project is funded by a state grant and transportation impact fees.

Stuart Mayor Sean Reed said the upgrades serve a critical purpose beyond capacity. "They're doing it to prevent storm damage during hurricanes and major storms," Reed said. "So the year of waiting will be worth it." With more than 1,400 boaters using the dock annually, the city is working to accommodate businesses and boaters during the closure. Austin Kuyrkendall, director of operations for Tiki Taxi & Cruises, said the city found a solution. "They're allowing us to build a gate right here at the end of the downtown Stuart dock. This is the non-floating section, but still we're going to be able to open this up and board people right here," Kuyrkendall said.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie advances plans for Midway Road Turnpike interchange, wider roads
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance last month to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to assist with a partial interchange at Midway Road and Florida's Turnpike.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance last month to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation for a partial interchange at Midway Road and Florida's Turnpike. Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, said the interchange addresses a significant gap between current Turnpike entrances and exits in the city. Samples noted the project is designed to accommodate growth already occurring and growth projected over the next 20 to 50 years.

The $95 million Midway Road Widening Project is currently in its first phase, with crews widening the road from two lanes to four lanes between Selvitz Road and Jenkins Road. The second phase, from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road, is in the design phase with construction anticipated to begin in Summer 2027. FDOT is also improving the Turnpike bridge and designing a partial interchange, still in design phase. The project will add bike and pedestrian paths along with sidewalks. City council will vote on final approval to give the land at an upcoming meeting.

cards.headline: West Palm Beach to Palm Beach airport elevated transit system proposed to county
cards.teaser: Glydways, a California-based autonomous transit company, is proposing an elevated network of self-driving vehicles that would connect downtown West Palm Beach to President Donald J. Trump International Airport in less than 10 minutes.
cards.body:
Glydways, a California-based autonomous transit company, is proposing an elevated network of self-driving vehicles to connect downtown West Palm Beach to President Donald J. Trump International Airport, along with nearby Brightline and Tri-Rail stations. The company will present the proposal to Palm Beach County commissioners Tuesday for initial consideration. Small autonomous electric vehicles carrying four to six passengers would travel along a dedicated elevated guideway built above existing roads. The system would bypass traffic congestion, potentially cutting the trip between downtown and the airport to less than 10 minutes. Glydways estimates travel times of seven minutes or less between the convention center and airport and roughly one to two minutes between Tri-Rail and the convention center.

Senior Vice President Brian Gettinger said the system would cost "a small fraction" of a traditional light rail system while offering comparable capacity, referencing previous South Florida estimates of $400 million to $500 million per mile. Gettinger emphasized the service would be priced like public transit, not private rideshare. Funding could come from Palm Beach County, the City of West Palm Beach, the Florida Department of Transportation, federal transit grants and public-private partnerships. Tuesday's meeting is not expected to approve construction, but rather determine whether the county should formally evaluate the proposal. If commissioners move forward, the county could seek competing bids and begin discussions on routes, station locations, costs and financing.

hero.headline: Anthem denies breast cancer patient's reconstruction surgery hours before procedure
hero.teaser: Beth Clark, 48, was denied coverage for a breast reconstruction procedure less than 24 hours before it was scheduled. Her insurance company, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield, said the surgical mesh involved is still considered investigational.
hero.body:
Beth Clark, 48, received a diagnosis of invasive ductal carcinoma, the most common type of breast cancer, three months ago. She decided to undergo a full double bilateral mastectomy to eliminate any possibility of cancer returning. However, less than 24 hours before her scheduled reconstruction surgery, her insurance company, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield, denied coverage for the procedure. According to the denial letter, the surgery involving a surgical mesh called GalaFlex was considered investigational with insufficient proof that it improves patient health outcomes.

GalaFlex is a synthetic surgical mesh that has become contentious in breast reconstruction treatment. Although plastic surgeons favor it and the FDA has approved it for certain uses elsewhere in the body, it lacks FDA approval specifically for breast reconstruction and remains classified as an off-label, investigational treatment. In a 2023 letter to health care providers, the FDA maintained that the efficacy and safety of GalaFlex for breast cancer patients have not been determined. Anthem stated in response to Clark's case that the mesh does not currently meet the standards required for coverage under its medical policy and that patients retain the right to appeal such decisions.

Dr. Alicia Billington, Clark's plastic surgeon, uses GalaFlex mesh on most of her breast reconstruction patients. She contends that while no treatment is risk-free, the product produces fewer complications compared to other established options. Billington has become vocal about criticizing insurance denials, joining other doctors who are taking their frustrations public and calling out specific insurers. She emphasizes that existing published literature and data from plastic surgeons support GalaFlex as the gold standard in breast reconstruction with implants and is requesting that insurers review this evidence. Last year, after investigative reporting highlighted breast cancer patients' denial stories as part of a "Patient No More" series, Cigna became the first and only major insurer to begin approving GalaFlex for breast reconstruction.

Despite Anthem's denial, Clark proceeded with her reconstruction surgery using GalaFlex mesh a little more than a week after the initial rejection. Billington found an alternative mechanism to make the procedure possible. Clark emphasized that her decision to move forward was based on trust in her medical care team, who she said were seeing excellent results and outcomes in their patients. She and Billington continue challenging the denial. Additionally, a new bill has been introduced to modernize the Women's Health and Cancer Rights Act, the federal law designed to protect breast cancer patients from treatment denials during their cancer care journeys.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie advances plan for new Florida Turnpike interchange at Midway Road
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation for a partial interchange at Midway Road and the Florida Turnpike.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance last month to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to assist with a partial interchange at Midway Road and the Florida Turnpike. Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, said there is a significant gap between the entrances and exits to the Turnpike currently in the city. According to Samples, the interchange is designed to accommodate growth that has already occurred and growth expected over the next 20 to 50 years.

FDOT has been constructing the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project to address congestion and safety concerns. Crews are currently working on the first phase, widening the road from two lanes to four lanes from Selvitz Road to Jenkins Road. The second widening phase from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road is in the design phase with construction anticipated to begin in Summer 2027. FDOT is also improving the Turnpike bridge and adding a partial interchange, which remains in the design phase. The Midway Road Widening Project will also include bike and pedestrian paths along with sidewalks. City council will vote on final approval to give the land at an upcoming meeting.

cards.headline: Stuart's downtown dock closes Monday for $3 million renovation doubling slip capacity
cards.teaser: Stuart's downtown public dock closes July 6 for a $3 million renovation projected to be complete by next Fourth of July.
cards.body:
Stuart's downtown public dock will close July 6 for a $3 million renovation projected to be complete by next Fourth of July. The project will nearly double the dock's capacity, expanding from 18 to 44 slips for both motorized and non-motorized vessels. The renovation includes a 7,500 square foot fixed dock, a 1,400 square foot floating dock and a smaller floating platform. The project is funded by a state grant and transportation impact fees. Stuart Mayor Sean Reed said the upgrades are designed to prevent storm damage during hurricanes and major storms.

During the year-long closure, the city is working to accommodate businesses and boaters who rely on the dock. Tiki Taxi & Cruises, which operates off the dock, received city approval to build a gate at the end of the downtown dock's non-floating section for passenger boarding. Austin Kuyrkendall, director of operations for Tiki Taxi & Cruises, said the dock can get hectic on weekends when boats squeeze in to find spots. Boat captain Parker Fisher, who is based in Stuart, said the dock has needed work over the years and hopes the renovation includes more floating docks. More than 1,400 boaters use the dock annually.

cards.headline: Riviera Beach named only Florida city to receive 2026 All-America City Award
cards.teaser: Riviera Beach was named one of just 10 communities in the U.S. to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League and was the only Florida city selected this year.
cards.body:
Riviera Beach was named one of just 10 communities in the U.S. to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League, making it the only Florida city selected for the honor this year. The award was announced during the National Civic League conference in Denver and recognizes communities that bring residents, local government, businesses and organizations together to solve local challenges and create lasting change. Mayor Douglas Lawson said the city earned the award through a long-term effort to revitalize Riviera Beach and improve quality of life for residents. City leaders say the recognition reflects years of work focused on improving civic health, strengthening trust between residents and local government, and creating opportunities for the community to play a direct role in shaping the city's future.

Riviera Beach's application highlighted several programs including the Riviera Beach Youth Council, which helps high school students become involved in civic leadership and advocacy; the Citizens Leadership Academy, a civic education initiative with a 98% completion rate; and the Neighborhood Reclaim Home Rehabilitation Program, which provides mini-grants to help longtime homeowners make critical repairs. Councilwoman KaShamba Miller-Anderson said the award is a tribute to the heart and determination of residents. The All-America City Award has been presented annually since 1949 and is considered one of the nation's most respected civic honors.

cards.headline: Delray Beach golf training center delayed 3 months and costs owner $90,000 after contractor issues
cards.teaser: Tom Molen, owner of Tee Box, a new virtual golf training and performance center near Delray Beach along Jog Road south of Linton Boulevard, said the project was delayed three months after problems with the contractor hired to prepare the space.
cards.body:
Tom Molen, owner of Tee Box, a new virtual golf training and performance center preparing to open near Delray Beach along Jog Road south of Linton Boulevard, said the project was delayed by three months after problems with the contractor hired to prepare the space. Instead of opening on schedule in April, Molen said the project was constantly pushed off by the contractor. Even though the contractor was licensed, the work ultimately had to be redone, creating a costly domino effect. Molen estimates the issues cost him about $90,000, not including revenue lost during the delays or the added expense of bringing in another contractor to fix the problems. "It was double pay on a lot of things from electricians to HVAC to drywall," Molen said.

Molen worked with Code Pro of the Palm Beaches, which is warning property and business owners to thoroughly vet contractors before hiring them. Code Pro founder David Allan estimates 25% to 35% of homeowners and property owners face major issues with unvetted contractors. He recommends using Palm Beach County's online portal to verify whether contractors have the proper licenses and insurance before any work begins. According to Allan, the most common contractor complaints in Palm Beach County involve roofing, windows and air conditioning work. Despite the setbacks, Tee Box is preparing for its grand opening set for July 17.

cards.headline: Hobe Sound community raises funds after woman dies in deadly home fire
cards.teaser: Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside her Hobe Sound home. Friends have launched a fundraiser to help White's fiance Mark rebuild after the flames destroyed many of his and White's belongings.
cards.body:
Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside her home in Hobe Sound. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office point to an electrical issue as a possible cause. The fire remains under investigation. Her fiancé Mark learned of her death and contacted friends to share the news.

Friends have since launched a fundraiser to help Mark rebuild after the flames destroyed many of his and White's belongings. Nina Fenn, who knew White for eight years, described the home as being in a complete state of devastation. Fenn said White was a Christian woman who loved gardening and plants, played the piano, and was always the first to lend a hand. She also loved kids and people. The timing of White's death adds another layer of heartbreak, as her birthday is the Fourth of July and she passed just a few days before it. Fenn noted that Mark has already endured significant grief, having lost his one and only child, Jacob, tragically. White's memory will live on in the hearts of those who loved her, Fenn said.

cards.headline: Fourth of July cookout costs rise 4% this year, ground beef and buns up most
cards.teaser: A Fourth of July cookout for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4% from a year ago, according to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey.
cards.body:
A Fourth of July cookout for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4% from a year ago, according to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey. The survey points to inflation as the primary driver of increased costs. Ground beef prices are up 5.5%, while buns have risen 7.7%. Strawberries, impacted by a Florida frost, are up 12.4%. Ice cream prices have increased 5.3%.

Some items offer relief from rising costs. Potato prices are down this year, benefiting those planning potato chips and salads. Corn prices have fluctuated, though locally grown corn from the Glades can provide the best value. Budgeting expert Andrea Woroch recommends comparing prices across stores to find the best deals for items on your grocery list. She also emphasized the importance of reducing food waste, which begins with creating a meal plan.

hero.headline: Saint Andrew's Scots football targets state title after 10-2 season and district championship
hero.body:
The Saint Andrew's Scots are working through the summer with their eyes on a state championship when the 2026 fall football season arrives. Last season's 10-2 record and district title felt incomplete after the team fell in the second round of the playoffs, motivating the program to aim higher this time around.

Head coach Jimmy Robertson credits the strength of his senior class for the team's optimistic outlook. "Most of these seniors are four-year seniors," Robertson said. "If not the majority of them came from the middle school as well. So they know how things are run. They had a lot of success in their career, and hopefully their senior year is the best season that we've had." A veteran group returning with experience and winning history provides a foundation for the Scots to build upon as they chase a state title.

The program is raising the bar by scheduling tougher opponents this fall. Senior Jack Williams explained the thinking behind this approach: "We knew that we wanted to take our program to the next level. So we really have a challenging schedule for this year because we wanna compete. That's what we wanna do and we wanna take that next level, and it's by playing against really good teams that we do that and attract new people." The demanding schedule is designed both to test the team and to draw attention to the program.

For Saint Andrew's, success this season will ultimately be measured by playoff performance rather than the regular season record. Senior Jack Whelche emphasized that going undefeated in the season means nothing if the team continues to exit in the second round. "A better year is just gonna be going farther in the playoffs. Obviously we wanna go undefeated in the season, but that doesn't matter if we keep losing in the second round of the playoffs. We just gotta go farther than that, that's all that matters," Whelche said. The team is using summer workouts as fuel for their championship ambitions. Senior Edmyer St. Jean views the daily grind as preparation for the payoff when the season starts. "It just adds up every day as something like to look forward to. Work harder so we can see the results when we come off the season positive and break our record," St. Jean said. With a determined veteran class leading the way, the Scots believe this is their year to finally break through and compete for a state title.

cards.headline: Martin County maritime teams deploy two boats with medics for Fourth of July weekend
cards.teaser: Martin County Maritime Response Unit is deploying two boats with medics in the north and south parts of the county as hundreds of boaters hit the water for the Fourth of July weekend.
cards.body:
Lt. Brett Harry with Martin County Maritime Response Unit said his team is expecting hundreds of boaters to be on the water celebrating the Fourth of July weekend. The unit will have two boats with medics on standby stationed in both the north and south areas of Martin County. Harry said the teams are deployed to help anyone who needs assistance, whether it's a minor injury like a stubbed toe or more serious medical emergencies including cardiac events or potential spinal injuries.

Boaters like Brendan and Ashley Shannon were launching off the ramps on Friday at Sandsprit Park in Martin County with their young daughter and puppy. The Shannons said safety is their top priority when heading out on the water. Harry urged boaters to take responsibility for their own safety by keeping their eyes on the water, designating a driver, and packing life vests, whistles and flotation devices. "Just have fun and be safe," Harry said.

cards.headline: Martin County School Board fights recommendation to reinstate teacher suspended over Charlie Kirk comments
cards.teaser: The Martin County School Board is pushing back against a judge's recommendation to reinstate Matt Theobald, a social studies teacher at Spectrum Academy suspended last year following controversial social media comments about Charlie Kirk.
cards.body:
The Martin County School Board is fighting an administrative law judge's recommendation to reinstate Matt Theobald, a social studies teacher at Spectrum Academy since 2009, who was suspended following controversial social media comments about Charlie Kirk. In a Thursday court filing, the board argued that Administrative Law Judge Jodi-Ann Vanessa Livingstone erred in her recommendation, claiming "numerous findings ... are not based upon competent substantial evidence." The board's attorney contends that Theobald's Facebook post about Kirk, which labeled him as racist, misogynistic and a neo-Nazi, constituted a "serious offense" that justified his removal.

In her order issued last month, Livingstone cited a recent Florida Fifth District Court of Appeal ruling that found disciplining a teacher for personal Facebook posts made off school grounds, on personal equipment, with no student involvement, violated the teacher's First Amendment rights. She also recommended Theobald receive back pay and benefits. According to an investigation report, Theobald admitted writing the comments but stated they were posted on his mother's private Facebook page "within a discussion among personal acquaintances" and were not intended for public view. Theobald told WPTV the case raises questions about where the line is drawn for teachers speaking outside of school. The school board retains final authority on whether Theobald will be reinstated.

cards.headline: Lantana veteran gets lien removed and roof fixed after WPTV intervenes
cards.teaser: Stephen McCoy, a disabled and retired veteran in Lantana, turned to WPTV for help with a roofing contractor he said left him with unfinished repairs and a lien on his home.
cards.body:
Stephen McCoy, a disabled and retired veteran from Lantana, hired Seabreeze Roofing and Sheet Metal in Boynton Beach to replace his nearly 20-year-old roof before hurricane season. McCoy made six payments totaling more than $17,000 to the company but said two holes were left unfinished on the back of his home. After the company stopped responding to his calls, texts, and emails starting in January, McCoy visited the building two or three times in person without success.

Letters from Gulfeagle Supply then arrived warning that a nearly $7,000 lien had been filed against his home. The lien stated that Gulfeagle Supply had furnished materials to Seabreeze Roofing for McCoy's property but was never paid. WPTV investigative reporter Kate Hussey visited Seabreeze Roofing and spoke with the owner about the unpaid materials. Within an hour, Hussey returned to McCoy's home with a final waiver of lien signed by Gulfeagle Supply and notarized, lifting the lien. McCoy was also informed the contractor would send someone back to fix the roof. About an hour after receiving the waiver, McCoy sent WPTV a photo showing crews back on his roof completing the work.

hero.headline: Loggerhead Marinelife Center in Juno Beach offers sea turtle nesting season programs through September
hero.body:
Loggerhead Marinelife Center in Juno Beach is offering educational and interactive programs during peak sea turtle nesting season through September. The center said guests can participate in seasonal experiences including guided Turtle Walks, the Hatchling Discovery Program, Hatchling Releases, Tidal Tots and Plastic Free July Community Action Day. According to the center, the programs are designed to give visitors an opportunity to learn more about sea turtle conservation along one of the world's busiest sea turtle nesting beaches.

The center's Turtle Walk program allows participants to observe the nesting process while learning about sea turtle biology, conservation and ongoing research efforts. Educational demonstrations during the programs may include the use of red-light headlamps, amber lighting, night scopes and research tag scanning equipment. Loggerhead Marinelife Center said its education and research departments work together during nesting season to collect and analyze data related to nesting activity and hatchling success. Sea turtle nesting season in Florida typically runs from March through October. Registration information and program details are available through Loggerhead Marinelife Center.

cards.headline: North Palm Beach celebrates Fourth of July with fireworks and America 250 events
cards.teaser: North Palm Beach residents and visitors will celebrate Independence Day with a full day of family-friendly activities, live entertainment and fireworks at North Palm Beach Country Club and The Clubhouse on July 4.
cards.body:
The free community event includes a pool party, lawn games, live music, a barbecue buffet and a fireworks finale scheduled for 9 p.m. Organizers say this years event also recognizes Americas 250th anniversary, bringing an added sense of celebration to the annual holiday tradition in Palm Beach County.

The festivities begin with a community pool party from 11 a.m. at the country club pool area. Guests can enjoy a water slide, DJ entertainment, games and activities, food and beverages and a poolside satellite bar. Beginning at 4:30 p.m., families can take part in activities including cornhole, Connect 4, Giant Jenga, face painting and lawn games. Live music from Solstice Reign is expected to begin around 6 p.m.

Ashley Shipman, director of parks and recreation, said the golf course will offer one of the best locations to watch the fireworks display. The Clubhouse will also host a Fourth of July barbecue buffet from 4:30 p.m.

hero.headline: St. Petersburg selects $8.1 billion plan to redevelop Tropicana Field site around civic park and museum
hero.teaser: St. Petersburg Mayor Ken Welch selected The Burg Bid as the preferred plan to transform Tropicana Field and the Historic Gas Plant District into a mixed-use district centered on a 13-acre civic park.
hero.body:
St. Petersburg has chosen The Burg Bid, a proposal led by Blake Investment Partners and Related Group, as its preferred path forward for transforming Tropicana Field and the surrounding Historic Gas Plant District. The $8.1 billion plan would convert stadium parking and public land into a mixed-use neighborhood featuring housing, hotels, offices, retail, cultural institutions, workforce training, public art and entertainment venues. The development team proposes purchasing 58 acres of city-owned land for $275 million, valuing the full land package at $405 million when including $130 million in land the city would retain. They plan to deposit $20 million when a purchase and sale agreement is finalized.

The proposal centers on Samuel Davis Park, a 13-acre central green space designed to serve as a civic and cultural hub rather than organizing around a new stadium as previous plans had done. The park would anchor 18.5 acres of total public park space and house The Woodson African American Museum of Florida, a planned Museum of Public Art, a Discovery Center, event lawns, a playground, a splash pad, cafe areas, public art and a concert lawn. The Woodson would serve as "an anchor and a civic landmark for the Gas Plant District," positioned within Samuel Davis Park along a diagonal pedestrian corridor called the Legacy Link. The proposal heavily emphasizes the history of the former Gas Plant neighborhood, a predominantly Black community demolished decades ago to build the stadium. Plans include preserving the original gas tank footprint, restoring Booker Creek from its current state as a drainage ditch, and constructing nine bridges as a reference to the nine bridges that once connected the historic area. A reimagined Pinellas Trail would integrate with wide pedestrian paths and a community park along the creek.

The development calls for 3,600 income-restricted housing units built over 15 years, with 1,800 units in the Historic Gas Plant District and another 1,800 on complementary sites elsewhere in St. Petersburg. The plan also includes homeownership opportunities at discounts to market value through partner Blue Sky Communities, a Florida-based affordable housing developer. The district would be constructed in three phases lasting approximately five years each, with early development potentially beginning outside the Tropicana Field footprint before stadium demolition. The Rays' lease ends after the 2028 season.

Phase 1 would establish cultural and workforce anchors including the Woodson and the Collaboratorium, a workforce training and small-business development center operating as "St. Petersburg's Capital Factory." Phase 2 would develop new mixed-income neighborhoods and strengthen connections with adjacent districts. Phase 3 would complete the neighborhood with a 4,000 to 5,000-seat Resilience Event Center featuring 100,000 square feet of flexible space for concerts, performances and events, plus a Discovery Center and St. Pete Surf Wave attraction.

cards.headline: DeSantis allies accuse Lieutenant Governor Jay Collins' wife of running anonymous accounts attacking Governor
cards.teaser: Multiple X accounts were suddenly deactivated Friday after allegations surfaced that they were tied to Layla Collins, wife of Lieutenant Governor Jay Collins, a.
cards.body:
Multiple X accounts were suddenly deactivated after allegations surfaced that they were tied to Layla Collins, wife of Lieutenant Governor Jay Collins. The accusations came from prominent veterans of Governor Ron DeSantis' communications team, including Christina Pushaw, a communications specialist in the Governor's Office, and Jeremy Redfern, Deputy Chief of Staff to Attorney General James Uthmeier. Pushaw shared information posted by Promota CEO Robert Salvador showing the account @FSUdude01670 appeared connected to a phone number similar to a known number and email used by Layla Collins. Florida Politics obtained screenshots verifying this through two-factor authentication, which can be triggered when an individual attempts to access an account without the preset password or if the social platform deems the password compromised. Screenshots showed an access attempt triggered a message to an email address with letters starred out and to a phone number with only the last digits visible.

Pushaw identified a second account, @bobnamy1, that she said also appeared tied to Layla Collins. She noted the account's content consisted entirely of promoting Jay Collins and attacking people who did not endorse him, including the governor. Redfern corroborated the claims, posting that "The FSUDude account was tied directly to her personal cell phone number." Both accounts were deactivated after Pushaw and Redfern publicly leveled their criticisms. Florida Politics has requested comments from Jay and Layla Collins.

cards.headline: Secretary of State Cord Byrd asks court to keep Paula Stark off ballot after qualifying paperwork failure
cards.teaser: Secretary of State Cord Byrd is asking Leon Circuit Court to keep St. Cloud Republican Paula Stark off the ballot after she failed to submit required paperwork by the qualifying deadline.
cards.body:
Secretary of State Cord Byrd is asking a Leon Circuit Court to keep Republican Paula Stark off the ballot for House District 47, citing her failure to submit required paperwork by the June 12 qualifying deadline. Stark's incomplete materials were timestamped less than 30 minutes before noon that day. Five state employees submitted sworn declarations stating that Stark's treasurer and partner, Joel Davis, never submitted Form 6, a public disclosure of financial interests, nor was it accidentally returned with his other paperwork. Three weeks after the deadline, Stark still has not submitted the form. Election Records Division Bureau Chief Erica Ikay Reeve noted that Stark was one of 12 candidates who failed to properly submit Form 6, though half of those candidates corrected the issue and qualified anyway.

Byrd argued in his response that had Stark or Davis exercised care by questioning the missing form or submitted documents earlier, the error could have been caught. Reeve also cited Stark's history of campaign finance problems, including Davis filing a report over one month late, reporting excessive contributions, and maintaining an incorrect address on file. The state revoked Stark's Friends of Paula political committee in November over 16,000 dollars in unpaid fines from missed deadlines. If Stark is removed from the ballot, the August primary for House District 47 would feature only Democrats Jorge Figueroa and Anthony Nieves, representing the traditionally Democratic district spanning Osceola and Orange counties.

cards.headline: The Woodson African American Museum of Florida to reopen July 11 with Smithsonian-linked exhibition
cards.teaser: The Woodson African American Museum of Florida is set to reopen its newly renovated museum July 11 as part of its 20th anniversary celebration.
cards.body:
The Woodson African American Museum of Florida will reopen July 11 as part of its 20th anniversary celebration, coinciding with the opening of a Smithsonian-linked America 250 exhibition. The museum was selected as one of only three Florida organizations to present the "Many Voices One Nation — Our Community" exhibition.

The museum's reopening marks a significant moment as The Woodson enters a new chapter with expanded programming and a planned permanent home. The Burg Bid proposal, selected by St. Petersburg Mayor Ken Welch as the city's preferred path for redeveloping Tropicana Field and the surrounding Historic Gas Plant District, places The Woodson within Samuel Davis Park along a diagonal pedestrian corridor called the Legacy Link. According to CEO Thompson Whitney Blake's proposal, WJArchitects designed an architecturally distinctive permanent home for the museum. The Woodson would serve as an anchor and civic landmark for the Gas Plant District at a time when the institution is entering a new chapter with its renovated facility.

cards.headline: State revoked Paula Stark political committee over $16,000 in unpaid campaign finance fines
cards.teaser: The state revoked Paula Stark's Friends of Paula political committee in November over $16,000 in unpaid fines from missed campaign finance deadlines.
cards.body:
Election Records Division Bureau Chief Erica Ikay Reeve detailed years of paperwork problems with Paula Stark's campaign in a court filing. Treasurer Joel Davis filed a campaign finance report over one month late, reported excessive contributions, and has an incorrect address on file. Audits in the 2022 and 2024 cycles found inconsistent amounts transferred from the campaign account to the office account and a balance after termination. In the 2024 cycle, the failure to pay a late report fine upheld by the Florida Elections Commission was referred to debt collection for nonpayment in November 2025.

The state revoked Stark's Friends of Paula political committee in November over $16,000 in unpaid fines from missed campaign finance deadlines. Reeve said Stark still has not submitted Form 6, a public disclosure of financial interests required by the June 12 qualifying deadline for House District 47. Secretary of State Cord Byrd is asking the courts to keep Stark off the ballot, arguing through court filings that five state employees gave sworn declarations that Stark's treasurer never submitted the Form 6 nor was it accidentally handed back during the final hour of the qualifying window.

The district would feature Samuel Davis Park, a 13-acre central civic and cultural space that would anchor the development. The park would be part of 18.5 acres of total public park space and would include a permanent home for The Woodson African American Museum of Florida, a Museum of Public Art, a Discovery Center, event lawns, a playground, a splash pad, and a concert lawn.

The proposal emphasizes respect for the Historic Gas Plant neighborhood, a predominantly Black community razed decades ago. The plan preserves the original gas tank footprint within Samuel Davis Park and weaves historic references throughout the Legacy Link, a diagonal pedestrian corridor connecting City Hall with the Manhattan Casino and the Deuces District. Nine bridges over Booker Creek would echo nine bridges that once stood in the area and restore physical connections across the site. The proposal also calls for restoring Booker Creek itself, which had been reduced to a drainage ditch between parking lots and Tropicana Field, with a reimagined Pinellas Trail integrating wide pedestrian paths and a community park along the creek.

cards.headline: Attorney General James Uthmeier endorses Byron Donalds for Florida Governor
cards.teaser: Attorney General James Uthmeier has endorsed U.S. Representative Byron Donalds for Governor as the race to succeed term-limited Ron DeSantis takes shape.
cards.body:
Multiple X accounts tied to Layla Collins, wife of Lieutenant Governor Jay Collins, were suddenly deactivated after allegations surfaced about their connection to her. Christina Pushaw, a communications specialist in the Governor's Office, and Jeremy Redfern, Deputy Chief of Staff to Attorney General James Uthmeier, publicly identified the accounts. Pushaw shared information showing the account @FSUdude01670 appeared connected to a phone number and email used by Layla Collins, verified through two-factor authentication screenshots obtained by Florida Politics. Pushaw also identified a second account, @bobnamy1, that appeared tied to Collins. She noted the account content consisted entirely of promoting Jay Collins and attacking people who did not endorse him, including the governor.

Redfern confirmed the connection, posting that "the FSUDude account was tied directly to her personal cell phone number." Both accounts were deactivated after Pushaw and Redfern leveled their criticisms publicly. Notably, both Pushaw and Redfern previously served as Press Secretaries for Governor DeSantis. Redfern now works for Uthmeier, who has endorsed U.S. Representative Byron Donalds for Governor. DeSantis appointed Jay Collins as Lieutenant Governor last year, seemingly helping the former state Senator develop a statewide profile to run for Governor, though DeSantis has declined to endorse a preferred successor in the race.

hero.headline: Hobe Sound woman dies in Monday home fire as community raises funds for fiance
hero.teaser: Misty Dawn White, 46, died Monday in a fire at her Hobe Sound home. Friends have launched a fundraiser to help her fiance Mark rebuild after the flames destroyed their belongings.
hero.body:
Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside her Hobe Sound home she shared with her fiancé. The sheriff's office determined that an electrical issue was likely responsible for the blaze. The investigation into the fire remains ongoing.

Mark, White's fiancé, notified close friends about the tragedy. Nina Fenn, who had been friends with White for eight years, received a call from Mark with the devastating news. Following the fire, friends and community members have organized a fundraiser to assist Mark in rebuilding his life after the flames consumed many of his and White's possessions. Fenn visited the scene in the days after the tragedy to process her grief. "It's just a terrible shame and awful loss of life," Fenn said, describing the aftermath as "completely a state of devastation."

Fenn shared details about White's character and the qualities that made her special to those around her. White was a devoted Christian who enjoyed gardening, cultivating plants, and playing piano. Beyond her personal interests, she had a generous spirit and was always willing to help others. "She was always the first to lend a hand," Fenn said. "She loves kids; she loves her kids. She loves people." White's impact on her community extended beyond her immediate circle, touching the lives of many who knew her.

The timing of White's death has added profound sorrow to an already tragic situation. White's birthday fell on July 4, meaning she passed away just days before celebrating another year. Additionally, Fenn noted that Mark is grieving multiple losses. "Mark lost his one and only child, Jacob, and lost him tragically," Fenn said. "So, I just am trying whatever I can to support him." These compounding losses have made the fundraising efforts particularly meaningful as the community rallies around Mark during this difficult period. Fenn expressed confidence that White's legacy will endure through those who loved her. "She's always been a good soul to me. She'll always be in our hearts," Fenn said.

cards.headline: Martin County Maritime Response Unit deploys medics for Fourth of July boating weekend
cards.teaser: Martin County Maritime Response Unit is deploying two boats with medics on standby in the north and south parts of the county as hundreds of boaters hit local w.
cards.body:
Hundreds of boaters are hitting Martin County waterways this Fourth of July weekend, prompting the Martin County Maritime Response Unit to deploy two boats with medics on standby in the north and south parts of the county. Lt. Brett Harry said the teams will respond to emergencies ranging from stubbed toes to cardiac events and potential spinal injuries. The unit is prepared to assist anyone who needs help throughout the holiday weekend.

Boaters like Brendan and Ashley Shannon launched from Sandsprit Park in Martin County on Friday with their young daughter and puppy. The Shannon family said safety is their top priority when on the water. Lt. Harry is urging boaters to take precautions before setting sail, recommending they keep their eyes on the water, designate a driver, and pack life vests, whistles and flotation devices. "Just have fun and be safe," Harry said.

cards.headline: Martin County School Board fights judge's order to reinstate teacher suspended over Charlie Kirk comments
cards.teaser: The Martin County School Board is pushing back against a judge's recommendation to reinstate Matt Theobald, a Spectrum Academy teacher suspended last year for Facebook comments about Charlie Kirk.
cards.body:
Matt Theobald, a social studies teacher at Spectrum Academy since 2009, sparked controversy with Facebook comments labeling Charlie Kirk as racist, misogynistic and a neo-Nazi. In a Thursday court filing, the Martin County School Board argued that Administrative Law Judge Jodi-Ann Vanessa Livingstone erred in recommending Theobald's reinstatement, stating that "numerous findings ... are not based upon competent substantial evidence." The board's attorney contends that Theobald's Facebook post about Kirk was a "serious offense" and that removing him was appropriate.

In an order issued last month, Livingstone cited a recent Florida Fifth District Court of Appeal ruling that said disciplining a teacher for personal Facebook posts made off school grounds, on personal equipment, with no student involvement, violated the teacher's First Amendment rights. The judge also recommended Theobald be awarded back pay and benefits. According to an investigation report, Theobald admitted writing the comments about Kirk but said they were posted on his mother's private Facebook page "within a discussion among personal acquaintances" and were not intended for public view. The school board retains the final say on whether Theobald gets his job back, with no clear timeline for a decision announced.

hero.headline: Costco plans first Treasure Coast store in Port St. Lucie
hero.teaser: The retail warehouse chain Costco is planning to open its first location on the Treasure Coast in Port St. Lucie.
hero.body:
Costco is moving forward with plans to build its first store on the Treasure Coast in Port St. Lucie. The retailer has announced the development of a new warehouse location in the city, marking the first Costco warehouse to serve Martin, St. Lucie, and Indian River counties. The membership warehouse shopping model will arrive in the Treasure Coast region for the first time with this new location.

The timing of Costco's expansion to Port St. Lucie aligns with significant infrastructure development underway in the city. Port St. Lucie is working to expand Midway Road and add a partial interchange to Florida's Turnpike to accommodate growth and improve accessibility throughout the region. The Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance last month to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to assist with the interchange project. Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, noted that "there's a pretty significant gap between the entrances and exits to the Turnpike currently in Port St. Lucie." He explained that the interchange is designed to address accessibility needs and support the city's growth trajectory. "This is a way for us to try to accommodate the growth that's already occurred, but also the growth that will occur over the next 20 to 50 years," Samples said.

The Florida Department of Transportation is managing a $95 million Midway Road Widening Project to help reduce congestion and improve safety. Crews are currently working on the first phase, widening the road from two lanes to four lanes between Selvitz Road and Jenkins Road. The second widening phase, which will extend from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road, is still in the design phase with construction anticipated to begin in Summer 2027. Additionally, FDOT is improving the Turnpike bridge and working on a partial interchange that remains in the design phase.

While construction activity has been noticeable to residents, many recognize its necessity. Port St. Lucie resident Erin Scheumeister acknowledged the disruption but saw the value in the improvements. "We definitely needed it to be expanded," she said. "It'll be a lot better and easier to get to work." Beyond road widening, the Midway Road project will also add bike and pedestrian paths along with sidewalks to improve multimodal transportation options. The city council is scheduled to vote on final approval to transfer the land at an upcoming meeting. These infrastructure improvements, combined with Costco's arrival, signal significant development momentum for Port St. Lucie.

hero.headline: Fourth of July Cookout Costs Rise 4 Percent Across Florida
hero.teaser: Holiday meals for 10 people now cost $73.82, up from last year, according to a new national survey tracking inflation at the grocery store.
hero.body:
The cost of hosting a Fourth of July cookout for 10 people has climbed to $73.82 this year, representing a 4 percent increase from the previous year, according to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey. The rise reflects broader inflationary pressures affecting grocery prices across the state and nation. Several key items driving the increase stand out as particularly expensive compared to last year's prices.

Ground beef prices have jumped 5.5 percent, while hamburger buns rose even more sharply at 7.7 percent. Strawberries have been hit especially hard, with prices climbing 12.4 percent due to damage from a Florida frost that affected the state's crop. Ice cream, a popular dessert at summer gatherings, has also become more expensive with a 5.3 percent price increase. These rising costs are forcing many families to reconsider their holiday meal planning and budgets.

Not all food prices have increased, however. Potato prices are down this year, offering relief to shoppers looking for affordable sides like potato chips and salads. Corn prices have shown more volatility throughout the season, though locally grown corn from the Glades region can provide better pricing options for budget-conscious shoppers. Finding these deals requires some strategy and attention to what's available in local markets.

According to budgeting expert Andrea Woroch, families can take several steps to manage cookout expenses without sacrificing quality or variety. She recommends shopping strategically by comparing prices across different stores to identify the best deals for items on your grocery list. Creating a meal plan before shopping is another effective approach, as it helps families avoid impulse purchases and unnecessary spending. Woroch also emphasizes that cutting down on food waste is crucial for keeping overall costs in check. By planning meals carefully and using ingredients efficiently, families can offset some of the price increases and still enjoy a festive Fourth of July celebration without breaking the bank.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County Schools Earn Third Consecutive A Rating
cards.teaser: The School District of Palm Beach County received an A rating from the Florida Department of Education for the third straight year, with 84 percent of district schools earning A or B grades.
cards.body:
The School District of Palm Beach County earned an "A" rating from the Florida Department of Education for the third consecutive year, reflecting strong student performance across all grade levels. The district achieved a record 93.5 percent graduation rate, with 143 district schools, or 84 percent, rated "A" or "B," up from 120 schools the previous year. District leaders reported that 86 percent of seniors participated in college-level coursework, taking at least one Advanced Placement, International Baccalaureate, Cambridge Advanced International Certificate of Education, or Dual Enrollment course. Additionally, 144 recent graduates earned an associate degree alongside their high school diploma.

S.D. Spady Elementary School in Delray Beach made a dramatic improvement from a "C" rating to an "A" this year. Principal Rona Tata, who has served as principal for 15 years after five years as assistant principal, credited the turnaround to curriculum modifications made three years ago. The school modified its early childhood curriculum program, which serves students starting at age 3 and combines with kindergarten. Many of those students are now in third grade and performing at higher levels. Three other district schools also improved from "C" to "A" ratings: Dwight D. Eisenhower K-8, Glade View Elementary, and West Gate Elementary.

cards.headline: Riviera Beach Named Only Florida City to Win 2026 All-America City Award
cards.teaser: The City of Riviera Beach is one of just 10 communities nationwide to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League.
cards.body:
The City of Riviera Beach received the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League, becoming one of just 10 communities in the U.S. selected for the honor and the only Florida city chosen this year. The prestigious award recognizes communities that bring residents, local government, businesses and organizations together to solve local challenges and create lasting change. The announcement came during the National Civic League conference in Denver, where Riviera Beach leaders presented the city's efforts to strengthen community engagement. Mayor Douglas Lawson called the recognition a proud moment, saying "Little old Riviera Beach is one of the biggest, brightest, shining stars." Lawson credited the city's long-term effort to revitalize Riviera Beach and improve quality of life for residents.

Riviera Beach's application highlighted several civic engagement programs, including the Riviera Beach Youth Council, which helps high school students become involved in civic leadership, the Citizens Leadership Academy with a 98 percent completion rate, and the Neighborhood Reclaim Home Rehabilitation Program, which provides mini-grants to longtime homeowners for critical repairs. Councilwoman KaShamba Miller-Anderson credited residents for the honor, stating the award reinforces the city's positive momentum and brings back community pride. The All-America City Award has been presented annually since 1949 and is considered one of the nation's most respected civic honors.

cards.headline: Juno Beach Council to Discuss Fence Replacement at JB-7 Beach Access
cards.teaser: Residents at the Colony Condos say people using the JB-7 public walkway are cutting through their private property since the town removed a fence in 2023.
cards.body:
Residents at the Colony Condos in Juno Beach say people using the JB-7 public walkway have been cutting through their private property since the town removed the old fence in 2023 for safety reasons. Without the fence, only bushes separate the public access path from private land. Lori Hill, a Colony resident, said the problem peaks in summer when visitors park in private spots and push through bushes with coolers, fishing rods and lawn chairs. Hill said residents used to confront trespassers directly, but confrontations became rude, so they now call the police to address the issue.

The dispute came before the Juno Beach Town Council at a recent meeting, where a town official noted the town is not obligated to install a fence. Vice Mayor Pro Tem DD Halpern suggested exploring a lower-cost solution, proposing a combination of split rail fencing and shrubs. Hill said residents are hopeful the town will reinstall the fence to protect their landscaping and private parking. The council agreed to address the fence question during its upcoming budget discussions on July 15.

cards.headline: Saint Andrew's Scots Football Targets State Title After 10-2 Season
cards.teaser: The Saint Andrew's Scots finished last season with a 10-2 record and a district title but lost in the second round of playoffs.
cards.body:
The Saint Andrew's Scots are preparing for the 2026 fall football season with their sights set on a state title. After finishing last season with a 10-2 record and a district title, the team fell short in the second round of playoffs, leaving them feeling like more was within reach. Head football coach Jimmy Robertson said most of the seniors are four-year seniors who came up through the middle school program and know how the program operates. "Most of these seniors are four-year seniors. I mean, if not the majority of them came from the middle school as well. So they know how things are run. They had a lot of success in their career, and hopefully their senior year is the best season that we've had," Robertson said.

The Scots have scheduled more challenging opponents this fall to compete at a higher level. Senior Jack Williams explained the reasoning behind the tougher schedule, saying the program wants to take itself to the next level by playing against really good teams. For the team, improvement this season is measured by one metric: advancing further in the postseason. Senior Jack Whelche said going undefeated in the regular season does not matter if the team keeps losing in the second round of the playoffs. The team is embracing summer workouts as motivation for the upcoming season.

cards.headline: Boca Raton High School Band to March in National Independence Day Parade
cards.teaser: The Boca Raton Community High School band will represent Florida at Washington D.C.'s National Independence Day Parade on July 4.
cards.body:
The Boca Raton Community High School band has earned an invitation to march in Washington, D.C.'s National Independence Day Parade on July 4 at 10:30 a.m., representing Florida. The students will march one full mile along the National Mall, traveling from Constitution Avenue to Independence Avenue. Only bands nominated by state officials receive invitations to this prestigious event.

Junior Lola Cabezas acknowledged the scale of the performance, noting that millions of people will be watching. She explained the physical demands of marching band, saying students must play, breathe, and walk while maintaining consistent sound. Senior Stephin Restivo said the team is focused on the marching and timing, knowing everyone will be able to see their performance. Band Director Jenn Girdlestone expressed confidence that students will represent the country well. Senior Lily Schaffer said making the trip to D.C. shows how much the program has grown. The parade will be streamed live on YouTube.
